done.why: The trap door locked behind me, and every exit from the cellar and troll room was blocked or marked unfinished.

about: A cut-down version of Zork. You collect things from the house, go down to the cellar and kill the troll. Beyond that the underground is unfinished.

moments.note: I typed 'take leaflet and read it' and was told 'You can't see any such thing'. I had just opened the mailbox, so it should have been visible.
Going down, the trap door crashed shut and was barred, which trapped me.
The troll was in a room just north of the cellar, and my sword killed him in one blow.
The east passage had a note pinned to the rock: 'Back soon. -- The Management.' It was a dead end.
The score was already 35 of 350 after 17 moves.

wished: Get back up the trap door, or find some other way out.

lines.line: The passage to the east has not been finished. A note is pinned to the rock: "Back soon. -- The Management."
lines.why: It told me the world stops here.

lines.line: From somewhere beyond it comes the sound of digging, which stops, politely, until you have backed out.
lines.why: A charming line that hints at work still going on beyond the rock.

fun.why: The opening was quick and satisfying, then I hit dead ends.

engagement.why: I had a clear goal, but I ran out of places to go very soon.

difficulty.why: The puzzles were easy, but I got trapped with no way out.

interestingness.why: The changed layout, with the troll right next to the cellar, was a pleasant surprise.

prose.why: The prose is mostly familiar, with a few witty new lines.
